criteria.text: Qualifying diagnosis attested by the closed indication selection
Patient is at least 5 years old
Ages 5–17: IV infusion only; ages 18 and older: IV infusion or subcutaneous injection
Prescribed by or in consultation with a rheumatologist, immunologist, nephrologist, neurologist, or dermatologist
Prescribed by or in consultation with a nephrologist or rheumatologist
Positive antinuclear antibodies (ANA) and/or anti-double-stranded DNA (anti-dsDNA) antibodies
ISN/RPS biopsy-proven active Class III or IV lupus nephritis alone or in combination with Class V
Currently receiving standard immunosuppressive therapy (hydroxychloroquine, chloroquine, prednisone, azathioprine, methotrexate) or has a contraindication to standard therapy
Currently receiving standard immunosuppressive therapy (azathioprine, mycophenolate mofetil, cyclophosphamide) or has a contraindication to standard therapy
Not taking concomitantly a biologic DMARD or Lupkynis
No severe active central nervous system lupus

notes: Partial encoding from Alaska Medicaid Benlysta (belimumab), a B-lymphocyte stimulator (BLyS)-specific inhibitor. Version 2; Original: 12/20/21; Effective: 11/1/22.

Closed indication selection attests to diagnosis. Both approval sections allow ages 5–17 with IV infusions only and ages 18 and older with IV or subcutaneous administration. The FDA summary describes lupus nephritis in adults; the pediatric IV path follows the explicit Alaska approval criteria. Standard therapy or contraindication is separately attested for each indication.
Duration (notes only): initial approval up to 4 months; reauthorization up to 12 months if the prescriber documents disease improvement.

Quantity and dosing (manual review): IV 120 mg or 400 mg vials, 10 mg/kg at weeks 0, 2, 4 then every 4 weeks. Subcutaneous 200 mg/ml prefilled autoinjector/syringe for active lupus nephritis: 8 injections in the first 28 days, then 4 injections per 28 days. HCPCS: J0490.

Cautions (notes only): use caution with severe or chronic infections; serious and sometimes fatal infections have occurred. Evaluate new or worsening neurological signs and symptoms for progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (PML). Consider premedication for infusion and hypersensitivity reactions. Assess depression and suicidality before treatment and monitor during treatment.

FDA limitations: efficacy has not been evaluated in severe active CNS lupus; not studied with other biologics and use is not recommended in these situations. Subcutaneous dosing has not been evaluated and is not approved below age 18 in this source.
PDL status unknown: source is silent. Therapeutic class retains the stub value other. Lupkynis is linked as an LN peer requiring separate eligibility evaluation, not concomitant use.
Remaining gaps: duration, reauthorization disease-improvement documentation, weight-based dosing, quantity enforcement and cautions require manual review.
